A logic circuit has three input bits: $a, b$, and $c$, where ' $c$ ' is the least significant bit and ' $a$ ' is the most significant bit. The output from the circuit is $1$ when its input is any of the $3$-bit numbers $1, 4,5,$ or $6;$ otherwise, the output is $0.$ Which of the following expressions represents the output from this circuit?
  1. $\overline{a}+\overline{b}+\overline{c}$
  2. $\overline{a} c+a \overline{b}$
  3. $\overline{b} c+a \overline{c}$
  4. $\overline{a} b c+a \overline{b}$

Consider $16$-bit binary representation of decimal number $\text{“53"}.$ It is stored in a system, which has byte-addressable memory where word size is $2$ bytes, beginning at address $100$ in big-endian fashion. What would be the content of location addressed by $101,$ in binary? (At bit-level we use big-endian)

  1. $00110101$
  2. $00000000$
  3. $10101100$
  4. $01010011$

  2. Writing the data back to cache, in addition to writing data to a register
  3. Writing data to the disk after doing a write to memory
  4. None of the above

  2. Absolute addressing mode
  3. Indirect addressing mode
  4. Register addressing mode

Assume that you have a page reference string for a process. Let the page reference string have length $p$ with $n$ distinct page numbers occurring in it. Let $m$ be the number of page frames that are allocated to the process (all the page frames are initially empty). Let $n>m$. Which of the following is correct? (Your answer is independent of the page replacement scheme that you use.)

  1. $p$ is the lower bound on the number of page faults.
  2. $n$ is the lower bound on the number of page faults.
  3. $p$ is the upper bound on the number of page faults.
  4. $n$ is the upper bound on the number of page faults.

Which of the following statements is/are False?
  1. Two processes reading from the same virtual address will access the same contents.
  2. Two processes reading from the same physical address will access the same contents.
  3. The size of a virtual page is identical to the size of a physical page.
  4. The OS provides the illusion to each thread that it has its own address space.

Which of the following statements is/are False?
  1. Stacks are used for procedure call frames, which include local variables and parameters.
  2. A SJF scheduler may preempt a previously running longer job.
  3. If all jobs have identical run lengths, a RR scheduler (with a time-slice much shorter than the jobs’ run lengths) provides better average turnaround time than FIFO.
  4. The longer the time slice, the more a RR scheduler gives similar results to a FIFO scheduler.

Which of the following statements is/are True?

  1. When a user-level process wishes to call a function inside the kernel, it directly jumps to the desired function.
  2. On a uniprocessor system, there is only one ready process at any point in time.
  3. The convoy effect in FIFO scheduler occurs when high-priority jobs must wait for lower-priority jobs.
  4. The OS provides the illusion to each process that it has its own address space.

Assume three jobs arrive at approximately the same time, but Job A arrives slightly before Job B, and Job B arrives slightly before job C. Job A requires $2$ sec of CPU, Job B is $8$ secs, and Job C is $7$ secs. Given a FIFO scheduler, what is the turnaround time of job B?

  1. $0$ seconds
  2. $2$ seconds
  3. $8$ seconds
  4. $10$ seconds

Given a disk with $200$ tracks, where track requests are received in the following order $55,58,39,18,90,160,150,38,184$. The starting position for the arm is track $100.$ What is the number of tracks crossed when the Shortest Seek First algorithm is used?

Which of the following addresses in decimal can not be the starting address of the word in a system with word size of $8$ byte, If word alignment is implemented?
  1. $1024$
  2. $2048$
  3. $1004$
  4. $2008$

A certain architecture supports indirect, direct, and register addressing modes for use in identifying operands for arithmetic instructions. Which of the following cannot be achieved with a single instruction?
  1. Specifying a register number in the instruction such that the register contains the value of an operand that will be used by the operation.
  2. Specifying an operand value in the instruction such that the value will be used by the operation.
  3. Specifying a memory location in the instruction such that the memory location contains the value of an operand that will be used by the operation.
  4. Specifying a memory location in the instruction such that the value at that location specifies yet another memory location which in turn contains the value of an operand that will be used by the instruction.

Consider the following decimal numbers. Which of the following decimal numbers Do Not have an exact representation in binary notation?
  1. $\text{U} = 0.1$
  2. $\text{V} = 0.3$
  3. $\text{X} = 0.4$
  4. $\text{Z} = 0.5$

  1. Instruction immediately following the branch condition

  3. Instruction that belongs to a different a subroutine
  4. It waits till the branch condition is evaluated
What is the minimum number of bits that are required to uniquely represent the characters of English alphabet? (Consider upper case characters alone)

$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline \textbf{Job} & \textbf{Arrival Time} & \textbf{CPU burst} \\
\hline \text{A} & 0 & 10 \\

Which scheduler uniquely minimizes the completion time of the entire workload?

  1. FIFO

  3. SRTF

Consider two different machines. The first has a single cycle datapath (i.e., a single stage, non-pipelined machine) with a cycle time of $15 \mathrm{~ns}$. The second is a pipelined machine with $5$ pipeline stages and a cycle time of $3 \mathrm{~ns}$. What is the speedup of the pipelined machine versus the single-cycle machine assuming there are no stalls?

Consider two different machines. The first has a single cycle datapath (i.e., a single stage, non-pipelined machine) with a cycle time of $15 \mathrm{~ns}$. The second is a pipelined machine with $5$ pipeline stages and a cycle time of $3 \mathrm{~ns}$. What is the speedup of the pipelined machine versus the single cycle machine if the pipeline stalls $1$ cycle for $25 \%$ of the instructions?

Which of the following statements is/are True?
  1. Paging approaches suffer from internal fragmentation, which decreases as the size of a page decreases.
  2. TLBs are more beneficial with multi-level page tables than with linear (single-level) page tables.
  3. LRU with $\mathrm{N}+1$ pages of memory always performs strictly better than LRU with $\mathrm{N}$ pages of memory.
  4. FIFO with $\mathrm{N}+1$ pages of memory always performs worse than FIFO with $\mathrm{N}$ pages of memory.

Consider the following variation of Peterson’s algorithm:

$\textsf{Process} \;\textsf{P}_{\textsf{i}}:$

do {
    flag[i] = TRUE;
    turn = i;
    while (flag[j] && turn == j);
    <critical section>
    flag[i] = FLASE;
    <remainder section>
} while (TRUE);

Which of the following is true for this solution?

  1. Mutual exclusion is satisfied but deadlock is possible.
  2. Mutual exclusion is not satisfied and deadlock is possible.
  3. Mutual exclusion is satisfied and deadlock is not possible.
  4. Mutual exclusion is not satisfied and deadlock is not possible.

A system uses a simple linear page table to implement virtual memory. The virtual address space is $1 \mathrm{~GB}\; (30 \;\text{bits});$ the page size is $1 \mathrm{~KB}$; each page table entry holds only a valid bit and the resulting page-frame number; the system has a maximum of $2^{15}$ physical pages $( 32 \mathrm{~MB}$ of physical memory can be addressed at most). How much memory, in $\text{MB},$ is used for page tables, when there are $200$ processes running in the system?

Three concurrent processes $\text{P1, P2}$ and $\text{P3}$ are concurrently updating a shared variable $xyz$ (with initial value of $100)$ as follows:

  • $\text{P1}: \quad x y z=x y z+10$
  • $\text{P2}: \quad x y z=x y z-20$;
  • $\text{P3}: \quad x y z=x y z \ast 2$

When a process executes an instruction such as $a=b \# c$ then it read $b,c$ from memory, performs $b \# c$ then writes the result into the memory location of "$a$".

What will be the maximum value of $xyz$ after the execution of the three processes?

Three concurrent processes $\text{P1, P2}$ and $\text{P3}$ are concurrently updating a shared variable $xyz$ (with initial value of $100)$ as follows:

  • $\text{P1}: \quad x y z=x y z+10$
  • $\text{P2}: \quad x y z=x y z-20$
  • $\text{P3}: \quad x y z=x y z * 2$

When a process executes an instruction such as $a=b \# c$ then it read $b, c$ from memory, performs $b \# c$ then writes the result into the memory location of "$a$".
What will be the minimum value of $xyz$ after the execution of the three processes?

Let $\text{A, B, C}$ be three boolean variables. $\oplus$ and $\odot$ are exclusive-or(ExOr) and exclusive-nor(ExNor) operations respectively.
Consider the following statements:

  1. $(\text{A} \oplus \text{B}) \oplus \text{C}=\text{A} \oplus(\text{B} \oplus \text{C})$
  2. $(\text{A} \odot \text{B}) \odot \text{C}=\text{A} \odot(\text{B} \odot \text{C})$
  3. $\text{A} \oplus \text{B} \oplus \text{C}=\text{A} \odot \text{B} \odot \text{C}$
  4. $\text{A} \oplus \text{B} \oplus \text{C}=\overline{(\text{A} \odot \text{B} \odot \text{C})}$

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

  1. $1$ and $3$ only
  2. $2$ and $4$ only
  3. $1,2$ and $3$ only
  4. $1,2$ and $4$ only

if the state registers are initialized to state $000,$ or

If the state registers are initialized to state $111.$

Then the number of SCDF functions with $5$ boolean variables is?

In a certain pipelined processor a branch instruction can cause $2$ stalls if it is not dealt properly. We can avoid this penalty if a clever compiler can fill the immediate next $2$ slots with independent instructions.

Two compilers $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ generate code for this processor.

Compiler $\text{A}$ can fill the first delay slot $35 \%$ of the time and second delay slot $85 \%$ of the time. Compiler $\text{B}$ can fill the first delay slot $20 \%$ of the time and second delay slot $100 \%$ of the time. Assume that $30 \%$ of the instructions are branch instructions. What is the $\%$ of the improvement in CPI(Clocks Per Instruction) with compiler $\text{A}$ over compiler $\text{B}?$

  1. $0$
  2. $5$
  3. $10$
  4. $15$

Consider a processor with a four-stage pipeline $\text{(IF, ID, EX, and WB)}.$
The functionality of the stages of this pipeline is as follows :

  • $\text{IF}$ – Instruction fetch from instruction memory
  • $\text{RD}$ – Instruction decode and Register read
  • $\text{EX}$ – Execute-ALU cooperation for data $\&$ address calculation
  • $\text{WB}$ – Register write back

$$

& \text { L3: } \mathrm{R} 2=\mathrm{R} 4-25 \\
& \text { L4: } \mathrm{R} 4=\mathrm{R} 1+\mathrm{R} 3 \\
& \text { L5: } \mathrm{R} 1=\mathrm{R} 1+30

$$

  1. Number of write-read(WAR) dependency $=4$
  2. Number of read-write(RAW) dependency $=4$
  3. Number of write-write(WAW) dependency $=3$
  4. Number of write-read(WAR) dependency $=3$

When performing hardware integer arithmetic, we say that overflow has occurred when the mathematically correct result of a computation cannot be represented in the number of bits available for the type being used. Obviously, it is important to be able to detect when an overflow error has occurred.

For the following options, the bit-sequences are $16$-bit $2\text{'s}$ complement representations of (signed) integer values. For which of the following, an overflow occurs when the given two integers are added?

  1. $0111\; 1001\; 1011\; 1011 + 0011\; 1011\; 1110\; 1110$
  2. $1111\; 0111\; 0110\; 1001 + 1000\; 0001\; 0110\; 0100$
  3. $0001\; 1100\; 0110\; 1111 + 1111\; 0111\; 1110\; 1101$
  4. $1100\; 1011\; 1010\; 1101 + 0111\; 1111\; 0010\; 1111$

A system $\text{S1}$ spends $50 \%$ of its time on graphics processing, $30 \%$ of its time on physics computations, and $20 \%$ of its time on modeling the intelligence of a game. Consider the following solution to a problem known as the "Too much milk" problem which says that there shouldn't be more than one milk packet in the fridge. $\text{Thread A}$ and $\text{Thread B}$ buy the milk packet. If there is no milk packet in the fridge then either $\text{Thread A}$ or $\text{Thread B}$ can buy the milk and put it into the fridge.

We have a milk variable which is initialized to $0$ and it indicates the number of milk packets in the fridge. For synchronization and for achieving the goal of "never making milk $\geq 2$ ", we present the following solution where $\text{noteA}$ and $\text{noteB}$ are two shared variables for the purpose of synchronization.

Note that the buyMilk function will increment the milk variable.

$\textbf{Thread A}$

noteA = 1;
if (noteB == 0) {
    if (milk == 0) {
        buymilk();
    }
}
noteA = 0;

$\textbf{Thread B}$

noteB = 1;
if (noteA == 0) {
    if (milk == 0) {
        buymilk ();
    }
}
noteB = 0;

Which of the following is true for the above attempt/solution to solve the Too much milk problem?

  1.  This approach suffers from starvation.
  2.  This approach suffers from deadlock.
  3. The goal is Not achieved by this approach i.e. milk variable can have value more than $1.$
  4. The progress is Not satisfied.
